facts.raw_span: A 69-year-old woman
history of hypertension
stage IA estrogen receptor–positive and progesterone receptor–positive and ERBB/neu receptor–negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast
presented with blurry vision in both eyes
1 mg of anastrozole daily 6 months prior to her presentation
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/40 OD and 20/25 OS
Pupils were equal, round, and reactive without an afferent pupillary defect
Intraocular pressures were normal
mild cataracts in both eyes
parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in the right and left eyes
the crystalline deposits did not display autofluorescence, suggesting that they were not lipofuscin granules
Crystalline deposits located at the level of the outer plexiform layers with some extension into the inner nuclear area subfoveally

concepts.why: The patient's history of anastrozole use and the presence of parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes suggest anastrozole-induced crystalline maculopathy.
The patient's age and the presence of mild cataracts in both eyes are consistent with age-related cataract.
The patient's history of hypertension and the presence of blurry vision in both eyes suggest hypertension-related retinal disease.
The patient's history of breast cancer treatment and the presence of eye symptoms suggest breast cancer treatment-related eye disease.
The presence of parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes suggests crystalline retinopathy.
The patient's age and the presence of blurry vision in both eyes are consistent with dry age-related macular degeneration.
The patient's history of anastrozole use and the presence of parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes suggest anastrozole-induced retinal toxicity.
The patient's history of hypertension and the presence of cataracts in both eyes suggest hypertensive retinopathy with cataract.

rationales.F05: Anastrozole use is a known risk factor for crystalline maculopathy.
rationales.F10: Parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits are characteristic of crystalline maculopathy.
rationales.F12: The location of the crystalline deposits at the level of the outer plexiform layers is consistent with anastrozole-induced crystalline maculopathy.
